newsitem.title: JAPAN: No agreement in Japan-Taiwan talks over islands.
newsitem.headline: No agreement in Japan-Taiwan talks over islands.

text.p: Japan and Taiwan on Friday failed to agree on fishing rights and other issues arising from a sovereignty dispute over a group of islands in the East China Sea, a Taiwanese official in Tokyo said.
"These are issues that can never be resolved overnight, and no agreement has been reached," Chuang Ming-yao, head of Taiwan's representative office in Tokyo, told reporters.

Chuang was speaking to reporters through an interpreter after he and other negotiators from Taiwan's foreign ministry, interior ministry and Council of Agriculture held a five-hour meeting with their Japanese counterparts in Tokyo.
During the talks, delegates from the two sides discussed fishing rights and other issues stemming from rival claims to a group of uninhabited islands in the East China Sea.
Chuang said the two sides did not decide when they would hold the next round of negotiations.

The two countries held their first round of talks in Taipei in August, a month after a simmering dispute exploded over ownership of the islands, known as the Senkakus in Japanese and as the Diaoyus in Chinese.

Japanese rightists raised their national flag and built a lighthouse on one of the disputed islands in July to assert Tokyo's claim, triggering an angry and increasingly nationalistic backlash from Chinese around Asia.
But Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda, citing a concern for international relations, announced on Friday that Japan would not formally recognise the makeshift aluminium lighthouse as a legitimate one.

Taiwanese fishermen complain that Japanese patrol boats have barred them from fishing near the islands claimed by Tokyo, Beijing and Taipei. Japanese patrols also have repulsed boats trying to land protesters from Taiwan and Hong Kong on the islands.
Japan, which recognises Beijing's communist government, has no diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
